messages:
Jamal: heads-up — spotted CVE-2026-9007 in github.com/infra/jwt-utils (token parsing overflow). SBOM flagged it for inference-serving and devex libs. CVSS: preliminary 7.8, EPSS lookup shows 0.085. any immediate owners?
Beatrice: :eyes: adding inference-servicing team, but quick q — is this reachable from hosted API or only internal pipelines?
Alex: quick surface-level check — our dependency tree shows jwt-utils pulled by auth-client v2.1.0 and session-middleware in runtime. hosted API uses auth-client in the edge proxy. likely reachable.
Maria: initial triage: CVSS 7.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N). EPSS 0.085 means moderate chance. No confirmed public exploit yet but PoC gist referenced in discussion thread.
Jamal: ok, treat as high for Hosted. suggest immediate mitigations: 1) pin to safe version if available 2) temporary WAF rule to block suspicious jwt payload length 3) emergency rollout plan for Dedicated to switch to compat-token-checker.
Alex: can we hotpatch runtime quickly? we have a small sanitization hook we can inject pre-parse. snippet for smoke test: ```python
# quick guard
if len(token) > 4096:
    raise ValueError("token too long")
```
Beatrice: prefer patching dependency; vendor released 1.2.1 with fix. plan: staged bump in Hosted canary => 5% (eu-west) then 25% then global if no regressions. for Dedicated, notify customers and provide mitigation steps.
sec-bot: Automated EPSS check: CVE-2026-9007 EPSS score 0.085 (data: 2026-03-20). No known exploit code in our telemetry.
oncall-bot: Canaries ok to schedule. use deploy-window: 03/21 0200-0400 UTC for low-traffic.
Maria: action items: 1) Jamal take Hosted canary (5%) and WAF rule 2) Alex prepare hotpatch branch and smoke tests (run on inference-serving) 3) Beatrice coordinate customer advisory for Dedicated 4) I'll own final CVSS/EPSS scoring and postmortem template if needed.
Alex: running quick grep to confirm binary reachability: ```bash
grep -R "jwt-utils" /srv || true
# found in /srv/edge-proxy/lib/auth-client
```
Jamal: audit logging check — KMS keys unaffected but need to search for anomalous Verify calls in last 72h. Maria, can you run a log query?
Maria: running now, query: ```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM auth_logs WHERE event = 'verify' AND created_at > now() - interval '72 hours' AND length(payload) > 2000;
``` results will be up in 8m.
Beatrice: if we see any large verifies spike, escalate to incident. otherwise follow staged bump. I'll draft customer note: short, technical, mitigation steps + timeline.
Jamal: tagging owners: @Beatrice @Alex @Maria. please update thread with smoke results and deploy status. :thumbsup:
Maria: quick update — no anomalous large payloads in last 72h. count=2 (within normal). proceeding with canary.
Alex: hotpatch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/472 — includes sanitization + unit tests. smoke run passed on canary instance. :shipit:
Beatrice: canary at 5% (eu-west) deployed, monitoring metrics (error-rate, latencies, token-reject-rate). will move to 25% in 30m if stable.
sec-bot: Vulnerability record created: RDW-INF-2026-042. severity: High. SLA target for mitigation: 72h.
Jamal: thanks team. final note — once global rollout done, schedule a short retro and add a test for oversized tokens to our regression suite.
Beatrice: acked. closing loop after 25% step and full rollout. :white_check_mark:
